My research is about finding structure in complex nonlinear systems and using it to predict them. I
come from computational fluid dynamics and geophysics, and now work mostly at the meeting point of
dynamical systems, data analysis and quantum-mechanical ideas. Papers are listed on the
[Publications](publications.qmd) page.

## Data-driven modeling and machine learning

Observations of climate, neural activity or turbulent flows are high-dimensional and noisy. I work on
ways to reduce them to a few meaningful spatiotemporal patterns and to use those patterns for
prediction, including extended-range forecasting of the El Niño–Southern Oscillation and the
identification of the Madden–Julian Oscillation.

## Operator-theoretic methods for nonlinear dynamics

Instead of following individual trajectories, operator-theoretic methods study how a system acts on
observables. Koopman operators and their spectra give a linear description of nonlinear dynamics,
which can be learned from data with kernel methods, tensor networks and exterior calculus. I use these
tools to separate trends, cycles and modes of variability in the climate system, and to analyse
non-autonomous and skew-product systems.

## Quantum-mechanical approaches and quantum computing

The same operator framework connects classical dynamics to quantum mechanics. I work on embedding
classical systems in quantum computers, on second quantization of classical nonlinear dynamics, and on
quantum-mechanical closure and data assimilation, where a quantum formalism is used to model the
unresolved scales of a classical system.

## Climate and complex systems

My earlier work in atmospheric science covers multiscale interactions in the tropics, cloud and
precipitation processes in large-eddy simulations, and the climate response to volcanic eruptions. The
same methods now reach beyond climate to plasmas, sea ice, neuroscience and astrophysics.

## Current projects

- **Data-driven analysis and prediction of weather-to-climate phenomena** — a computational toolkit
  based on operator-theoretic techniques. DOD grant, 2024–2027, as Co-PI.
  [Project website](https://nh24-8392.github.io/public-website/).
- **Quantum information science and Koopman operator theory for plasmas** — improved modeling and
  understanding of plasmas. DOE grant, 2024–2027, as Co-PI.
